L55: > Récoltes et Semailles, A. Grothendieck
L56: Addressing A. Grothendieck’s extensive body of published works involves key considerations. Initially, while Grothendieck’s mathematical and literary reflections spanned his entire life, it was only the active period from 1950 to 1969 that saw traditional forms of regular publication. Post this phase, publishing his works became sporadic and complex. Additionally, at present, a wealth of unpublished material holds potential for posthumous publication.
L57: With these aspects in focus, the CSG is committed to enhancing accessibility and collaborating with publishing houses to effectively study, catalog and enlarge A. Grothendieck’s body of published works. This endeavor aims to formally categorize and grant citability to all of Grothendieck’s publications in a unified fashion.
L58: While more sophisticated readers who are familiar with Grothendieck’s main contributions will be most interested in the unpublished works, even within the realm of these published works, their classifications, and posthumous additions, these experts might come across novel or less familiar items.
L59: Furthermore, by meticulously compiling Grothendieck’s entire body of publications in categories, we offer readers the opportunity to place his works within contexts of interest, thus fostering potential avenues for new research.

L9:   * 【5†Motives letter to Serre (August 8, 1964)】- The English translation of a letter from from Grothendieck to Serre which contains his first written mention of motives. The original letter is published in Correspondance Grothendieck-Serre, Documents Mathématiques, Société Mathématique de France, 2001.
L10:   * 【5†Crystals letter to Tate (May 1966)】 - A 31-page letter from Grothendieck to Tate, in which the notion of crystals was born and baptized (with a nice ``commentaire terminologique'' about the name). It contains the conjectures, based on an analogy with the work of Monsky-Washnitzer in the affine case, on the comparison between crystalline and de Rham cohomology.
L11: For a first-hand historical survey of the theory (starting with the present letter), see the article by L.Illusie in Motives, Proceedings of Symposia in Pure Mathematics, Volume 55, 1994, Part 1, 43-70.
L12:   * 【5†Motives letter to Illusie (May 3, 1973)】- A letter from Grothendieck to Luc Illusie containing remarks on motives. The original letter is published as an appendix to an article by Jannsen, in Vol. I (p. 296) of Motives (U. Jannsen et al. eds), Proc. Symp. Pure Math 55, AMS, 1994.

L16:   * 【4†Anabelian letter to Faltings (June 27, 1983)】 - A typed-up version of a letter from Grothendieck to G. Faltings in German, describing Anabelian Algebraic Geometry. To Grothendieck's disappointment, Faltings never responded to this letter. However, Faltings' student Shinichi Mochizuki picked up the subject years later and proved Grothendieck's anabelian conjecture for hyperbolic curves.
